tasks.title: Arranging an online language exchange
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.text: Read this email from your new language exchange partner, Yuki, and the notes you have made.

promptBlocks.subject: Our first language exchange!
paragraphs: Hi! I'm really excited to start our language exchange. I think we should have a weekly call to practise. What day and time works best for you?
Also, I'd like to choose an activity for our first call. I was thinking we could talk about our favourite films or maybe play an online word game. Which do you prefer? Why?
Finally, do you have a preference for which platform we use – Zoom, Skype, or something else? I want to make sure it's easy for both of us.
Let me know what you think! Best, Yuki

promptBlocks.heading: Notes for your reply
listItems: Suggest a weekly time and day.
Choose an activity and give a reason.
Answer her question about the platform.
Ask Yuki if she has any language goals for the exchange.

promptBlocks.text: Write your email to Yuki using all the notes.

tasks.title: Communicating well online
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.heading: Articles wanted!
paragraphs: How can teenagers communicate clearly and respectfully online?
Write an article for our student website giving advice.
- How can you make sure your messages are easy to understand?
- What should you do if you disagree with someone online?
The best articles will be published on our website!

tasks.title: The wrong message
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.text: Your English teacher has asked you to write a story.

promptBlocks.label: Your story must begin with this sentence:
promptBlocks.text: As soon as I pressed send, I realised the message was meant for my best friend, not my teacher.
